A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICQF study and contain complete, readable main text and appendices A–I. Pages 3–32 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; the differences are confined to pages 1–2.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic questionnaire experiments and CBCL analyses using HBN and ABCD, including diagnostic prediction and factor-loading stability results (Section 4, Tables 1–2, Figure 3).

after.justification: v3 retains these original synthetic and clinical experiments, their quantitative results, and the supplementary factorization results and clinical assessments in the appendices.

M1.justification: The ICQF objective, constraints, confound handling, ADMM/FISTA and coordinate-descent procedures, and BCV factor selection are unchanged (Section 3; Appendices A–B).

E1.justification: The synthetic questionnaire scenarios and CBCL evaluations using HBN and ABCD are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same 21-questionnaire coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: ℓ1-NMF, FA-promax, syndrome subscale scores, and the dimensionality-selection schemes listed in Table 1. Comparator participation is unchanged in Figure 3 and Table 2.

E3.justification: The BCV design, data splitting, training-size comparisons, logistic-regression evaluation, and AUC and correlation metrics are unchanged (Sections 3–4; Appendix E). No experimental settings are revised.

E4.justification: The synthetic noise tests, sample-size sensitivity analyses, cross-study factor-loading comparisons, and expert assessments of clinical factors are retained unchanged (Section 4; Appendices G–I).

E5.justification: Both retain 30 generated synthetic datasets, 30 seeded clinical dataset splits, standard-error and standard-deviation reporting, Figure 3's 95% confidence regions, and the same Wilcoxon tests and false-discovery-rate adjustment.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 1–8, including appendix findings, are identical. For example, Table 2 retains the ICQF cross-study loading correlation of 0.75 with standard deviation 0.07.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, Propositions 3.1–3.2, optimization derivations, and proofs in Appendices A–D are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and Discussion retain the same scientific claims about interpretability, convergence, factor selection, diagnostic information and stability. The Python-implementation contribution already appears in v2; v3 supplies its package address.

C2.justification: Explanations of regularization, confound modeling and clinical factor structure, along with applicability qualifications and future research directions, are unchanged (Sections 3–5; Appendix I).

D1.justification: Introduction contribution 4 in v3 adds an explicit, clickable GitHub address for the standalone ICQF package: github.com/jefferykclam/ICQF. v2 mentions a Python implementation without this address or an equivalent embedded package link. Other technical and reproducibility details are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography, and the positioning of ICQF relative to factor analysis and NMF are identical. No related work is added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 appends one package-access sentence to Introduction contribution 4 and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose, terminology and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions and their placement are unchanged throughout both PDFs. The added sentence fits the existing final text line on page 2 without changing the page layout.

improvement.justification: v3 supplies a direct package link where v2 only mentions the Python implementation, improving code discoverability and reproducibility documentation. The scientific content, results, theoretical arguments and appendices are unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
